ask: C11, POSIX. progress.c: reusable ANSI progress bar — determinate and indeterminate modes, throughput and ETA estimation with exponential smoothing, terminal width detection via ioctl, carriage-return redraw, and a demo loop over 200 items. write the file.
prose:
`progress.c` written (11014 bytes). Build and run:

```sh
cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -o progress progress.c && ./progress
```

A few notes on the implementation:

- `progress_update` takes the absolute completed count each call, so you can skip items or call it at irregular intervals without drift.
- ETA switches to elapsed time once `current >= total`, so the final frame shows how long it actually took.
- The bounce width in indeterminate mode is 25% of the available bar — wide enough to read at a glance but not so wide it looks stuck.
- `terminal_width()` re-queries `TIOCGWINSZ` on every draw, so resizing the terminal mid-run is handled cleanly.

To embed it in another project, pull out the `progress_t` typedef, the three public functions (`progress_init`, `progress_update`, `progress_finish`), and their helpers — everything above `main`. The `main` demo can be dropped or kept as a smoke test.
